rv.q: After more than three and a quarter hours, though, we’re used to the sight. Annie Baker’s drama arrives from New York trailing plaudits and a Pulitzer, but I do wonder whether we’d permit such over-indulgence in a home-grown product.
This is a play rich in humour and insight that reveals its purpose slowly but to devastating and memorable effect.

Annie Baker’s Pulitzer winning play THE FLICK an off Broadway hit arrives at the National Theatre this spring. Running at three and a half hours, this story about a falling Massachusetts cinema and the people who work there proves to be a hard watch, yet it’s strength comes from pioneering and unusual directorial choices.
